q: Fill up: In India, abortion is defined as termination of pregnancy before ______ weeks of gestation or the birth of a fetus weighing less than ______ g.
exp: Indian law uses the 28-week or 1000 g definition of viability, so expulsion before that limit and weight is called abortion.

q: All of the following infections are associated with spontaneous abortion EXCEPT:
opts: Human papillomavirus infection of the cervix
Listeria monocytogenes infection
Treponema pallidum infection
Cytomegalovirus infection
exp: Cervical HPV causes warts and neoplasia, not pregnancy loss; listeria, syphilis, CMV, rubella, toxoplasma and parvovirus all cause loss.

q: Fill up: The commonest cause of a sporadic first-trimester abortion is a ______, and the single commonest chromosomal abnormality found is ______.
opts: chromosomal anomaly; autosomal trisomy
uterine anomaly; triploidy
luteal deficiency; monosomy X
maternal infection; tetraploidy
exp: About half of early losses are chromosomally abnormal, with autosomal trisomy the commonest abnormality, followed by monosomy X and polyploidy.

q: Match the endocrine cause with its association — 1) Poorly controlled diabetes 2) Luteal phase deficiency 3) Thyroid autoimmunity … A) Loss is linked to thyroid antibodies even when thyroid function tests are normal B) Losses occur mainly in the first trimester, so control before conception matters most C) Progesterone support helps only in selected women with recurrent loss
exp: Diabetic loss tracks glycaemic control at conception, thyroid antibodies mark risk independent of function, and progesterone has a narrow role.

q: All of the following are part of the standard evaluation of recurrent pregnancy loss EXCEPT:
opts: Partner karyotyping after a single first-trimester loss
Lupus anticoagulant and anticardiolipin antibody testing
Thyroid function, prolactin and glycaemic assessment
Three-dimensional ultrasound or hysteroscopy for a uterine anomaly
exp: Investigation begins after three consecutive losses (or earlier if indicated); a single sporadic loss needs no work-up.

q: Fill up: A cervical length below ______ mm before 24 weeks is taken as evidence of cervical weakness, and the measurement must be made by ______ sonography.
opts: 25; transvaginal
30; transabdominal
15; transvaginal
25; transabdominal
exp: Transvaginal measurement is the standard; an empty bladder, a full-thickness view and a short closed cervix below 25 mm mark risk.

q: Which of the following statements about cervical incompetence is TRUE?
opts: It is essentially a clinical diagnosis of painless second-trimester dilatation with recurrent mid-trimester losses
A cervical length above 30 mm on transvaginal scan confirms the diagnosis
It classically presents with painful contractions and heavy bleeding in the first trimester
It is diagnosed by measuring serum progesterone in the middle of the second trimester
exp: Painless dilation with recurrent second-trimester loss is the hallmark; ultrasound supports the diagnosis but does not define it.

q: A 28-year-old at 20 weeks with two previous mid-trimester losses has membranes bulging through a cervix dilated to 3 cm. She has no contractions, no bleeding and no fever. What is the management?
opts: Rescue or emergency cerclage after excluding infection, with antibiotics, tocolysis and corticosteroids
Immediate induction of labour, because exposed membranes cannot be saved
Discharge with bed rest and no intervention, since the cervix is already dilated
Vaginal progesterone alone, because no suture can be placed once membranes bulge
exp: Rescue cerclage is worthwhile in selected women once infection is excluded and membranes are reduced, though benefit is smaller than with elective cerclage.

q: All of the following are true of transabdominal cervico-isthmic cerclage EXCEPT:
opts: It is placed vaginally and the suture is removed at 37 weeks
It is chosen when the cervix is very short, scarred or a vaginal cerclage has failed
Delivery must be by caesarean section, since the suture cannot be removed
It is usually placed before pregnancy or in early pregnancy, often laparoscopically
exp: Transabdominal cerclage is placed at the cervico-isthmic junction from above and commits the woman to caesarean delivery.

q: Match the cerclage with its technique — 1) McDonald 2) Shirodkar 3) Transabdominal … A) A purse-string suture at the cervicovaginal junction placed without any dissection B) A submucosal tape at the level of the internal os placed after reflecting the bladder C) A suture placed at the cervico-isthmic junction from above, usually by laparoscopy
exp: McDonald is the simple purse-string, Shirodkar needs bladder reflection to reach the internal os, and the abdominal route is reserved for failed or impossible vaginal cerclage.

q: Fill up: Elective cerclage is typically performed at ______ weeks of gestation, and the suture is removed at ______ weeks.
exp: Elective cerclage is placed once viability and anatomy are confirmed around 12-14 weeks and removed near term before labour begins.

q: All of the following contraindicate cervical cerclage EXCEPT:
opts: A previous uncomplicated term delivery with no history of pregnancy loss
Active vaginal bleeding or ruptured membranes
Chorioamnionitis or evidence of intrauterine infection
Lethal fetal anomaly or intrauterine fetal death
exp: Cerclage is contraindicated by bleeding, rupture, infection and fetal death; a woman with no history suggesting weakness simply does not need one.

q: Fill up: Antiphospholipid antibody syndrome is diagnosed when a clinical criterion is combined with persistently positive ______, ______ or ______.
opts: lupus anticoagulant; anticardiolipin antibody; anti-beta2 glycoprotein I antibody
antinuclear antibody; anti-dsDNA; anti-Sm antibody
rheumatoid factor; antinuclear antibody; anti-CCP antibody
lupus anticoagulant; antinuclear antibody; anti-dsDNA
exp: The three criteria antibodies are lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin and anti-beta2 glycoprotein I, each needing confirmation 12 weeks later.

q: Match the antiphospholipid test with how it is performed — 1) Lupus anticoagulant 2) Anticardiolipin antibody 3) Anti-beta2 glycoprotein I … A) A phospholipid-dependent clotting test such as the dilute Russell viper venom time B) IgG or IgM measured by ELISA, medium or high titre, above the 99th centile C) IgG or IgM measured by ELISA, above the 99th centile, confirmed 12 weeks later
exp: Lupus anticoagulant is a functional clotting assay, while anticardiolipin and anti-beta2 glycoprotein I are ELISA-based and all need repeat confirmation.

q: Which of the following statements about antiphospholipid syndrome in pregnancy is TRUE?
opts: Thrombotic risk is highest in the puerperium, so thromboprophylaxis is continued for six weeks after delivery
Risk returns to normal the moment the placenta is delivered, so prophylaxis can stop at delivery
Low-molecular-weight heparin must be replaced by warfarin throughout the first trimester
Low-dose aspirin and heparin are contraindicated in pregnancy because of the risk of fetal bleeding
exp: Heparin does not cross the placenta and with low-dose aspirin is the standard treatment; postpartum thromboprophylaxis is essential.

q: A 26-year-old at 9 weeks has light vaginal bleeding and a closed cervical os. Ultrasound shows a live embryo with a small subchorionic haematoma. What is the appropriate management?
opts: Reassurance and avoidance of strenuous activity, since no drug or bed rest has been shown to change the outcome in most cases
Immediate evacuation of the uterus to prevent heavy haemorrhage
Urgent cervical cerclage, since first-trimester bleeding indicates cervical incompetence
High-dose intramuscular progesterone continued throughout the pregnancy
exp: Most threatened abortions continue; intervention is reserved for inevitable, incomplete or missed abortion and for heavy bleeding.

q: Match the type of abortion with its findings — 1) Threatened 2) Inevitable 3) Incomplete … A) Bleeding and pain with a dilated os and membranes that may rupture B) Partial expulsion of products with an open os and heavy bleeding C) Bleeding with a closed os and a live fetus, so the pregnancy may continue
exp: Threatened abortion has a closed os and a live fetus, inevitable abortion has a dilated os, and incomplete abortion has retained products.

q: Fill up: Missed abortion is diagnosed when the mean sac diameter is above ______ mm with no embryo, or the crown-rump length is above ______ mm with no heartbeat.
exp: These thresholds prevent the tragic error of diagnosing pregnancy loss from a scan that is simply too early to show the embryo.

q: All of the following describe grade III septic abortion EXCEPT:
opts: Infection confined to the uterine cavity with no systemic signs
Peritonitis with infection spreading beyond the pelvis
Septic shock with hypotension and oliguria
Endotoxic shock with renal cortical necrosis or disseminated intravascular coagulation
exp: Grade I infection is confined to the uterus, grade II spreads to the pelvis and parametrium, and grade III means peritonitis, shock or organ failure.

q: Fill up: Under the MTP (Amendment) Act 2021, termination up to ______ weeks needs the opinion of one registered medical practitioner, and termination between ______ weeks needs two.
exp: Up to 20 weeks one registered medical practitioner suffices; from 20 to 24 weeks two are required for the specified categories of women.

q: Which of the following statements about consent under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act is TRUE?
opts: The woman's own consent is required, and for a minor or a woman with mental illness the written consent of a guardian is needed
The husband's signature is mandatory before any termination can be performed
Two registered medical practitioners must examine every woman even when the pregnancy is under 12 weeks
Consent is unnecessary when the woman is unmarried, since the guardian decides
exp: The Act protects the woman's autonomy: her consent governs, with guardian consent only for minors and women with mental illness.

q: Match the method with its role — 1) Mifepristone 2) Misoprostol 3) Manual vacuum aspiration … A) Prostaglandin analogue given 24-48 hours later to expel the products of conception B) Antiprogesterone given first, which primes the cervix and detaches the decidua C) The preferred surgical method up to 12 weeks, suitable for an outpatient setting
exp: Mifepristone sensitises the uterus to prostaglandin, misoprostol expels the pregnancy, and manual vacuum aspiration is the surgical option in the first trimester.
